title: openai-compat-selection-contract-and-deterministic-tool-frames
author: Diego Alvarez
release_notes: Adds a formal selection contract for OpenAI compatibility, deterministic streaming frames for tool outputs, per-request selection mode, and migration tooling. Default behavior remains backward-compatible (permissive).
description: Background: The OpenAI compatibility layer must behave deterministically for customers that rely on single-tool selection and streaming reassembly. We observed multiple customer integrations where ambiguous tool_choice tokens and non-deterministic stream fragments caused incorrect dispatch and failed reassembly under packet reordering. This change introduces a portable selection contract and deterministic framing for tool messages to make downstream consumers resilient. What changed: 1) Selection contract: a compact contract formalizing how the adapter exposes model-declared tool choices to the router. Three modes are supported: permissive (legacy behavior, first-match), strict_single_choice (model must provide a single explicit tool_choice field; otherwise response is rejected), and advisory (model suggestions are annotated but do not gate dispatch). Modes can be set per-request via the header X-Redwood-OpenAI-Selection or via route config. 2) Mapping stage: explicit tool_schema_mapper converts internal tool descriptors to OpenAI-style function schemas and emits stable schema_id tags. Mapper supports schema_overrides and preserves custom vendor metadata with a vendor_meta field. 3) Deterministic frames: streaming encoder now emits small, self-describing JSON frames with fields: role, schema_id, seq_num, eof, and payload. Frames include a stable schema_id and incremental seq_num so consumers can reassemble even when fragments arrive out of order. The framing protocol is documented and opt-in via openai_compat.streaming_frame_mode: off|stable-json|compact. 4) Reassembly and idempotency: the framer attaches a frame_checksum and an optional message_hint to help downstream idempotent processors ignore duplicates. 5) Backpressure and pacing: when models request multiple tool invocations concurrently, the dispatch router enqueues candidacies into a soft-queue sized by openai_compat.max_concurrent_tool_invokes and applies a paced-launch strategy to avoid burst overload on dedicated pools. Rejections emit metric openai.compat.tool_enqueue_rejected and a standardized OpenAI-style error object with type rate_limit.error. 6) Migration & tooling: added CLI command redwood openai-compat migrate-tools that introspects registered handlers and writes a suggested schema_override file; added lint command redwood openai-compat lint-schemas which flags ambiguous unions and missing required fields. 7) Tests and docs: added unit and integration tests for out-of-order frame reassembly, multi-tool suggestion paths, and rejection/fallback behavior. Updated openai-compat.md with protocol examples and a migration checklist. Compatibility and rollout: default selection mode stays permissive. strict_single_choice is behind an opt-in flag openai_compat.enable_strict_single_choice and requires operator confirmation to flip in the console to reduce accidental breakage. For Dedicated clusters the selection_mode can be set via cluster config and propagated over redis. Implementation notes: key changes in src/compat/openai_mapper.py, src/streaming/framer.cc, src/dispatch/tool_router.rs, cli/compat_migrate.py, docs/openai-compat.md. This PR does not change model server kernels or KV cache layout.
